# temps_survey (Resource)

An in-app survey the project's analytics script shows to visitors matching `targeting`.

Import with `<project_id>/<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `surveys:read`, `surveys:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_survey" "nps" {
  project_id = temps_project.web.id
  name       = "NPS"
  status     = "draft"
  questions  = jsonencode([{ id = "q1", kind = "nps", prompt = "How likely are you to recommend us?" }])
  targeting  = jsonencode({ path_pattern = "/pricing*", sample_rate = 0.25, once_per_visitor = true })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the survey.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the survey asks about.
- `questions` (String) Questions: `jsonencode([{ id = "q1", kind = "nps", prompt = "How likely are you to recommend us?" }])`. Kinds: `open_text`, `rating`, `nps`, `single_choice`, `multiple_choice`. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.
- `status` (String) Only `active` surveys are shown. One of `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `completed`.
- `targeting` (String) Who sees it: `jsonencode({ path_pattern = "/pricing*", sample_rate = 0.5, once_per_visitor = true })`. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<project_id>/<id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>/<id>
terraform import temps_survey.nps 8/2
```
